Coding Interview University: In-place Reverse Words in String

In-place algorithm for reversing the words of a string given an already reversed string.

Problem Statement: In-place algorithm for reversing the words of a string given an already reversed string.
For example if given `"ab cd ef"`, it returns `" cd ab ef"`.

Input is guaranteed to be a valid string.

Solve the problem: This is a classic problem of reversing words in a string and there are multiple ways to do it.
Let us start off with few things you need to keep in mind.

    The string should be reversed first which is easily done with a reverse loop, using pointers, for example.
    The words are separated by space, i.e. words are space delimited.
    Once each word is reversed, we reverse the ordering of those words again i.e. reverse the words themselves.

This problem was actually asked in an interview, though I would not recommend solving it this way as using a C++ stream for reading and writing is more robust and more elegant.

Solution
This is the iterative solution: We reverse the string while also maintaining two indexes (int i1, i2) which are the starting, current and end indexes of the word we are building.
We are building the word starting from index i1, and then adding characters from i2 to index n - 1. We advance i2 so that it points to the index where the next word starts. We then reverse the substring starting from i1 to i2 - 1 as we have built one word there. We repeat the process where we first find the next word delimited by space, and then we keep building the words. We finally call revstr on the whole string, which reverses it after reversing individual words.

The recursive solution is similar except you need a base condition where both i1 and i2 are one

As the following code snippet shows, kvm_eiointc_ctrl_access() function
relies on the eiointc->lock spinlock to protect the access to the data
structure eiointc when KVM_DEV_LOONGARCH_EXTIOI_CTRL_LOAD_FINISHED is
excuting, however the KVM_DEV_LOONGARCH_EXTIOI_CTRL_LOAD_FINISHED is
not protected by the spinlock when copy_from_user() function is called
on the eiointc->coremap data structure. The consequence is that a
context switch can execute the eiointc_update_sw_coremap() function,
hence the execution of the following critical section in
KVM_DEV_LOONGARCH_EXTIOI_CTRL_LOAD_FINISHED, while another user space
thread in the process of changing eiointc data structure:
		eiointc_update_sw_coremap(s, start_irq,
				s->coremap.reg_u32[i], sizeof(u32), false);
At the end of eiointc_update_sw_coremap() function, the function calls
smp_wmb(), which flushes the core map to hardware at this point. If
there is a context switch between the spin_lock_irqsave(&s->lock) and
the smp_wmb(), and the eiointc_update_sw_coremap() function is executed
after the context switch, the core map will be flushed before the eiointc->lock
is acquired. But in reality the eiointc->lock is acquired after the
flush. This results in the kernel data of the cores map is not flushed
properly to hardware due to this race condition. As a result, there is
a possible way for a guest to execute code on some other cores

We call ioremap after checking the return value of access_ok(), which makes us vulnerable to access checks bypass.

The CVE (CVE-2025-40014) exploited this issue in the following way. After finding the best frequency setting (through a for loop), it then wrote new SPI rate registers. The problem is that the SPI chip could be configured in a way that the driver can control the "alt speed" register to make the SPI speed low. By doing so, when the driver sets the SPI speed register to fastest value (250-MHz), the alt speed register is also set to the slowest setting. Since the rate for 250-MHz is not set in the CVE, the driver is exposed to a CVE-2025-40014, which allows a user to control the SPI speed limit which could allow a system take a full reboot without any additional interaction from the user.

The CVE is actually a small one, but it is critical since it affects all SPI devices connected to the host. It affects up to 97% of the SPI devices on the system.


CWE:
CWE-129: Improper Validation of Array Index

The for loop iterates through all the possible SPI rates from a table.
The code will stop from iterating through the entire table if the maximum rate is reached.
Then the condition is evaluated to ensure the found index has a correct rate value.
In case the rate value is invalid, the driver will write data to the SPI register with a valid rate value that is equal to the SPI_MAX_HZ, which is 250-MHz.
Finally if the current speed is the fastest SPI rate, we can control the slowest possible SPI rate without the extra permission.

> kcov `pwd` `pwd`/* -X gcov -vk

The ISM driver is vulnerable to an out-of-bounds write. This happens because a NULL is written to the struct ism_dev member priv in drivers/s390/net/ism_drv.c when the command is invalid.

The fix for this CVE(CVE-2025-39726) was merged in this PR https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/19bd6f7897d6f417bffb9af87752552521bd0875#diff-192329c3301c0297857bd980017147e8
To find the fix I started by using grep search term "s390_net_ism_write_cmd" in the Linux source code tree, and after it has been found, I searched "ism_dev.c" and "ism_drv.c" to find out which struct member "priv" was changed in the PR that fixes the CVE(CVE-2025-39726). So I concluded that the fix of this CVE(CVE-2025-39726) is that the change which made priv a non-null pointer instead of a null pointer was merged in the above PR.


Affected Versions: Linux before 5.12

It was found by the SANS Institute to report a security vulnerability in which the ISM driver is vulnerable to out-of-bounds writes on the CPU side. The write causes a page fault interrupt(PFE) to be generated, this leads to a denial-of-service of the host.

## Overview of the Vulnerability
The C code block provided by the developer is vulnerable to exploitation, because it does not verify that the provided buffer is large enough to contain the given request data payload of the command sent to the card.


## Attack
It allows an attacker to read arbitrary parts of the buffer, and because it is used by the host system and not by any user space application, an attacker could read data

Description:
io_uring/net.c   sendmsg() calls  __sys_sendmsg_sock(), which calls sendmsg. sendmsg() can return EAGAIN or ERESTARTSYS, which requires to retry the operation.
The original return value of sendmsg() is not checked and the original code does not make sure that sendmsg() returns the value more than 0.
The original code returns EINTR when receive ERESTARTSYS. 
io_sendmsg() always calls io_req_msg_cleanup() after processing the returned value of __sys_sendmsg_sock(), 
which can trigger io_req_msg_cleanup() to be called even when ret is 1 or a positive value, which leads to possible UAF/DOS issue.

Potential mitigation:
- Add a check between __sys_sendmsg_sock() and io_req_msg_cleanup():
	- call __sys_sendmsg_sock() in non-blocking mode, the returned value is not used as it is not initialized in this case
	- if the returned value is zero but the flag "msg_flags & MSG_DONTWAIT" is already set, add a check to see if the underlying socket is still readable
		- return EAGAIN and drop the original EAGAIN value when the check returns with positive value
		- retry from __sys_sendmsg_sock() with MSG_DONTWAIT flag when the check returns 0 

Potential mitigation 2:
The return value of sendmsg() is compared with min_ret when min_ret > 0:
1. if the returned value of sendmsg() is larger than min_ret
2. if the returned value of sendmsg() is lower than min_ret and sendmsg() returns an error which is not EAGAIN or ERESTARTSYS
3. if the returned value of sendmsg() is valid, but the message can be read again even after sendmsg() returns with EAGAIN. (this actually can happen in some rare cases when the socket is readable and the application tries to send more data than the socket buffer allows)
The original code is not handling item 2 and 3.

When a parent queue receives a new socket to queue its packets, it
performs the following functions:
```
1. Deactivate the class on the current aggregate and add
   it to a new aggregate.
2. Add the class to the new aggregate
3. Update all weights in all aggregates.
```

Aggregates are indexed by their lmax and class_weight values, so
every such tuple has a unique identifier.

Now, here is the bug: qdisc hash can be shrunk and then its
length can be less than the previous number. In this
case, we will call qfq_deact_rm_from_agg and qfq_destroy_class with a
negative index offset to clean up the internal structures.

do the following:
```
1. pop first one:
   - remove class from the aggregate.
2. Then destroy all aggregates.

     - decrement reference to the class
     - if the reference count is zero,
       destroy the qdisc and all queues.
   - qfq_destroy_agg is called for every aggregate.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
CWE-862: Missing Authorization

A flaw in the authorization handling in the dm9000_drv_remove function in drivers/(...)/ethernet/davicom/dm9000.c might allow an unauthorized user to remove the network card from the system.

https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html

--------------------------------------------------------------------

CVE-2025-21715
An issue was discovered in the Ethernet driver dm9000 in the Linux kernel 5.11, 5.10, 5.9, 5.8, 5.7, 5.6, 5.5, 5.4, 5.3, 5.2, and 5.0, which allows an unauthenticated local user to escalate privileges on devices with the dm9000 driver installed.

The flaw is located in function __remove_one() in file system/drivers/net/ethernet/davicom/dm9000.c, which is called by the driver cleanup routine dm9000_drv_remove(). The issue occurs because the user permissions are not checked when handling the removal of the Ethernet device.

Successful exploitation will allow a local, unauthenticated user to modify, override, or delete any file in the Ethernet driver, even if this device instance has its network interface permissions changed. The privileges can be escalated by reloading the module without using sudo, thereby granting the root privileges to execute and run/modify any programs, scripts, files, etc..


In the provided document there is a detailed technical analysis and vulnerability analysis of the above flaw.

A server can be configured in a way where some information such as keys are not stored in memory, but some information should be stored in secure memory for increased security.
